source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Request an ethics committee consultation directly, per most facility policies, rather than being limited to informal peer discussion as the colleague is currently assuming","B":"Raise concerns mainly informally among coworkers, with little formal channel readily available to them, similar to what the colleague is currently assuming about this situation","C":"Address the concern mainly by first going through the attending physician before any other step, which understates the direct access this nurse actually has to a formal ethics consultation","D":"Generally be unable to raise an ethical concern about a client's care through any formal process, similar to what the colleague is currently assuming about the options available here"}}
source_row.rationale: Most facility policies allow any member of the care team, including nurses, to directly request an ethics committee consultation when they have an ethical concern about client care.
source_row.stem: A nurse has an ethical concern about a client's care, and a colleague assumes the only real option available is to informally mention it to coworkers since there's no accessible formal channel for this kind of concern.
